description: Every power- and torque-quantity input and result row (HP, WHP, kW, lb-ft, N·m, ft-lbs, and the power-based ratios) of the 696 calculators, scanned in Imperial and in Metric at default state, and classified against the platform unit convention locked in on 2026-10-13 (GH-IMP-013 philosophy, GH-IMP-019 plan). cls: engine-power = gasoline / diesel engine power (default HP in both systems); engine-torque = engine torque (default lb-ft in both systems); ev-power = EV motor / electric powertrain / battery power (default kW in both systems); ev-torque = EV motor torque (default lb-ft under the current convention); driveline-torque, road-load-power = rows whose engine-versus-component reading needs owner confirmation (conf = confirm); component-torque (fasteners, brakes, bearings, yaw moment) and non-engine-power (pumps, tire heat) = retained as system-governed (N·m / kW in Metric); converter = a converter's own result row, named for its own unit; engine-derived, power-to-weight, hybrid-engine-power, road-load-derived = ratios and splits built on power that need a decision (conf = decision), most of them the BSFC family. conflict = true when the current Metric behaviour differs from the intended one; imperial_now / metric_now are the units shown today, imperial_intended / metric_intended the units the convention calls for (null = decision needed). READ-ONLY INVENTORY: no calculator behaviour is changed by this file, and no test reads it yet. It is the evidence for GH-IMP-019 and the row list its regression test would pin. First generated from the engine dump at f2d8fb4 plus the GH-IMP-013 D1/D2 declarations (the D1/D2 commit c0241f8 changed no power or torque row: a fresh dump of the current engine matches every row). SECOND PASS (2026-10-13, GH-IMP-019): reconciled against the current engine (HEAD c28e934, engine sha256 9674a993...): 21 rows the first inventory could not see were added (see "added"); every original row and its original "cls" are unchanged. Each row now also carries the performance-unit POLICY fields: cat (named policy category or RETAIN-*), status (decided = fixed by the owner on 2026-10-13, recommended = awaiting approval, retain = keeps its own convention), inh (inherits the performance power / torque preference, or follows the system, or its own unit), default (what Auto resolves to), alts, mech (how the row is declared: convertible = a registered unit the table can re-tag; native = a raw kW box; unregistered; fixed-label = literal text in a simulator grid; converter), effect (what it touches: profile link, stored value, report), and for the ambiguous rows qty (physical quantity) and role. chg_imp / chg_met say whether the row's Auto display differs from today in that system. READ-ONLY EVIDENCE: no calculator behaviour is changed by this file and no test reads it yet.

implementation_check.by: GH-IMP-019 implementation (premium/tests/performance-census.test.js reads this file as its starting list)
added: sim_curve_editor IN curve_y_0 .. curve_y_11 declared HP (Power-vs-RPM mode; this file has the lb-ft variant of the same twelve boxes) - ENGINE_POWER
sim_acceleration, sim_dragstrip, sim_top_speed OUT 'Engine curve peak' lb-ft - ENGINE_TORQUE (literal text line of the Engine Curve block, outside the result helpers)
sim_acceleration, sim_dragstrip, sim_top_speed OUT 'Engine curve peak' HP - ENGINE_POWER (the same line for a power curve; reachable only through window._ghmCurveMode, GH-DEF-029)
spelling_notes: thermal_efficiency the_q (fuel-energy input) is spelled HP-equiv and shows kW-equiv when Power = kW
ev_motor_power has two rows labelled 'Motor Power': the kW row is EV_POWER, the HP companion row is RETAIN-ALT (does not follow the preference)
ohms_law OUT Power (W) and sim_curve_editor OUT Peak Power (HP) are drawn only in a stored mode
12 retained rows are drawn by hand-written markup, not by field() / resultHTML() / multiResult(): bsfc BSFC and 11 converter outputs
implementation_check.result_at_default_state_auto_auto: before/after of all 696 calculators in both systems against the engine of d776d21: 6,366 rows, 6,231 identical (118 retained-category rows included), 133 intended policy changes (Metric 128, Imperial 5), 2 rows moved by 2 parts per million (fuel_pump_sizing, rounded-text class), 0 unexpected

reconciliation.method: fresh DOM dump of all 696 calculators in both systems on the current engine compared row by row with the file (198 of 199 keyed rows identical, the 199th is a same-label second row added by hand); independent declaration scan (every field() / resultHTML() / multiResult() call, default state, every other option of every <select> once, and every stored mode toggle) compared the other way; label scan for power/torque-looking labels with other units: only dimensionless rows. Gaps found: W, lb-in, in-lb and PS units were outside the first unit list (16 rows in 14 calculators, all non-engine, one of them (ohms_law Power) only in the stored Solve-P mode); simulator output grids are literal text outside .result-box / .mini-result (5 rows).

ENGINE_POWER.meaning: gasoline / diesel engine output (flywheel / crank), also parasitic loads taken from the engine

EV_POWER.meaning: electric motor / electric powertrain output, battery power

EV_TORQUE.meaning: EV motor torque (lb-ft is the current product decision; one table cell to change)

WHEEL_POWER.meaning: power at the wheels and the drivetrain loss between crank and wheels (WHP culture)

ROAD_LOAD_POWER.meaning: power the vehicle needs for drag, rolling resistance, grade (read against engine hp); EV context would use EV_POWER

HYBRID_SYSTEM_POWER.meaning: combined system output of a hybrid powertrain

WHEEL_TORQUE.meaning: torque at the wheels / axle (calculated from engine or motor torque)

DRIVELINE_TORQUE.meaning: torque carried or rated by clutch, differential, driveshaft, axle (read against engine torque)

retained.RETAIN-COMPONENT: component torque / moment (fasteners, brakes, bearings, yaw): system-governed
retained.RETAIN-ACCESSORY: stand-alone accessory or thermal power (pump, tire heat, electrical W): system-governed or own unit
retained.RETAIN-CONVERTER: converter row named for its own unit: shows exactly the unit it is named for
retained.RETAIN-RATIO: ratio pinned to its own unit (Downforce per Added HP, water-methanol flow per hp)
retained.RETAIN-BSFC: brake specific fuel consumption: fuel mass per unit of engine work, system-governed until the ratio decision (O4)
retained.RETAIN-EMISSIONS: emissions per unit of energy (g/kWh): not a performance unit
retained.RETAIN-ALT: the optional hp companion row of ev_motor_power
retained.PTW_RATIO: power-to-weight ratio: power part follows the power preference, mass part follows the system (composite, O4)
